newsitem.title: USA: Oct. 17 debate set on best first pet.
newsitem.headline: Oct. 17 debate set on best first pet.

text.p: Some people may think all the hullaboo about the presidential debates is for the dogs.
A debate being sponsored Oct. 17 by the Humane Society of the United States is for the cats and dogs.
It will help raise money for the country's largest animal protection organisation and consider the burning question: Would a dog or a cat make a more suitable pet in the White House?

The debate, to be moderated by NBC-TV's John McLaughlin, host of the long-running "McLaughlin Group" programme, is co-sponsored by K-III Communications, which publishes both Cats Magazine and Dog World.
Socks, the Clinton family cat, currently resides at the White House, but Republican Bob Dole and his wife, Elizabeth, have a dog named Leader and they would like the dog to take the cat's place.
Contributing editors for the two magazines will head the respective debate teams.
The sponsors have opened two 900 phone lines to allow Americans to vote on the issue. Voting began on Sept. 25 and will continue until the presidential election on Nov. 5.
To vote for a cat as "First Pet," call 900-680-CATS; for a dog, call 900-680-DOGS. Each call costs 75 cents, with 25 cents from each call to be donated to the Humane Society, the organisers said.
The debate will take place in Washington in conjunction with the annual conference of the Humane Society.
